## [00:00 — 00:08] Segment 1

Welcome to our April research seminar on efficient and trustworthy language models.
Today we will survey recent advances across four key themes: memory efficiency,
inference speed, factual grounding, and alignment safety.

---

## [00:08 — 00:17] Segment 2

Sparse attention mechanisms dramatically reduce GPU memory consumption. By learning
which token pairs matter, models can scale to much longer contexts without proportional
memory cost.

---

## [00:17 — 00:26] Segment 3

Mixture-of-experts architectures enable model scaling without proportional inference
cost. Routing tokens to specialised experts allows very large total parameter counts
with manageable active parameters per forward pass.

---

## [00:26 — 00:35] Segment 4

Retrieval augmentation grounds model outputs in verifiable external sources. Rather
than relying entirely on parametric knowledge, retrieval-augmented models can cite
and reference specific passages, reducing hallucination.

---

## [00:35 — 00:44] Segment 5

Constitutional AI alignment uses self-critique to train models that evaluate and
revise their own outputs. By distilling this process into a compact reward model,
alignment can be applied efficiently at scale.

---

## [00:44 — 00:53] Segment 6

Federated learning distributes model training across devices, keeping sensitive data
local. Recent advances in differential privacy noise scheduling have substantially
closed the accuracy gap versus centralised training.

---

## [00:53 — 01:02] Segment 7

Neurosymbolic approaches bridge neural pattern recognition with symbolic execution,
enabling reliable compositional generalisation. Typed lambda calculus programs offer
a structured substrate for systematic reasoning.

---

## [01:02 — 01:11] Segment 8

Robust evaluation requires multiple benchmarks and ablation studies. Single-metric
optimisation often conceals failures on complementary tasks.

---

## [01:11 — 01:20] Segment 9

Key open challenges include cross-lingual generalisation, adversarial robustness,
and deployment under realistic resource constraints. No single method addresses all
challenges simultaneously.

---
